gap: No result ChatGPT got says that rumble, not button switches, can be the loudest thing a controller makes. EasySMX's own explainer says 'Strong rumble can create greater room noise than the buttons'. Both quiet picks let you turn it down without a PC: the X05 Pro uses M + Left Stick (Level 0 to 4), and the PS5 has Vibration Intensity and Trigger Effect Intensity under Settings > Accessories.
standout_why: I opened our current page (cited #1) and hlplanet's G7 Pro vs G7 SE vs Cyclone 2 page (cited, which gives membrane vs microswitch per model). hlplanet already makes the switch-type point: it calls the G7 SE 'Membrane (Quiet/Soft)' and the G7 Pro 'Optical Micro Switches', so the membrane vs microswitch idea is only partly new. Neither page mentions rumble or DualSense trigger effects as a noise source, and neither says how to turn them down. I could not open the cited Reddit threads (Reddit blocks fetches) or the cited Super Nova manual (manuals.plus PDF is image-only, no text layer). ChatGPT's answer says DualSense 'triggers can still make noise' but gives no fix.
decides: Keep the EasySMX X05 Pro as the top pick: EasySMX says it 'uses redesigned button mechanics and silicone damping' and Retro Handhelds lists its face buttons as 'Optimized Quiet' membrane. The page should add one setup line, though: quiet buttons don't help if rumble stays strong. On the X05 Pro, press M and push the Left Stick down to lower vibration. For the DualSense, set Vibration Intensity and Trigger Effect Intensity to Off in PS5 Settings > Accessories > Controllers. That keeps the DualSense as the quiet PS5 pick and fixes the trigger-noise caveat ChatGPT left open. The microswitch vs membrane split also backs leaving microswitch pro pads out (GameSir G7 Pro, Cyclone 2).

findings.label: Maker's explanation of what makes controller noise
findings.value: Button noise 'comes from switch type, damping, shell design, and pressing force'; 'Microswitch buttons often produce a clear click when activated'; 'Rubber membrane buttons usually sound softer' but can still make noise when the cap bottoms out
findings.source_title: Why Are Some Gaming Controllers So Loud? Quiet Buttons Explained (EasySMX blog, Peter Lai, 2026-08-06)
findings.note: Maker's own article. Gives no dB figures.

findings.label: Rumble as a noise source
findings.value: 'Strong rumble can create greater room noise than the buttons'
findings.source_title: Why Are Some Gaming Controllers So Loud? Quiet Buttons Explained (EasySMX blog)
findings.note: Same article. It also says bumpers 'may sound sharper because they use a shorter movement', triggers 'reach a physical stop', and L3/R3 'use switches below the stick assembly'.

findings.label: How the quiet buttons work (maker)
findings.value: 'uses redesigned button mechanics and silicone damping to reduce button noise'
findings.source_title: Why Are Some Gaming Controllers So Loud? Quiet Buttons Explained (EasySMX blog)
findings.note: The article does not say which inputs are left undamped.

findings.label: Vibration intensity control
findings.value: Press M + Left Stick up or down; 'Level 0 to 4 vibration intensity'; default is native vibration
findings.source_title: Questions about EasySMX® X05 Pro Controller (EasySMX support)
findings.note: Maker's FAQ, section Q8b. It does not say in words that Level 0 means off.

findings.label: Input types and noise (reviewer)
findings.value: Face buttons 'Optimized Quiet' membrane; D-pad tactile ('a really quiet clicky'); shoulders 'quiet, and they have a quiet click'; Hall Effect sticks and triggers; 'my unit has some creaking if you press too far'
findings.source_title: EasySMX X05 Pro review (Retro Handhelds, Ban, 2025-11-19)
findings.note: Named reviewer's hands-on impressions, not measured. The review does not cover stick-click (L3/R3) noise.

findings.label: Console settings that quiet the controller (maker)
findings.value: Settings > Accessories > Controller (General): 'Vibration Intensity' ('Set the intensity of the DualSense wireless controller vibration') and 'Trigger Effect Intensity' ('Set the intensity of the DualSense wireless controller trigger effect')
findings.source_title: Adjust general controller settings on PS5 (PlayStation Support)
findings.note: Sony's page names both settings but does not list their values.

findings.label: Off value for vibration and trigger effects
findings.value: 'Look for the Vibration Intensity option... Set it to "Off."' and 'look for Trigger Effect Intensity and set it to "Off."' (Settings > Accessories > Controllers)
findings.source_title: How to Turn Off Adaptive Triggers and Haptic Feedback on PlayStation 5 (SteelSeries, 2020-11-23)
findings.note: Named third-party guide, used because Sony's own page does not list the Off value. The guide dates from 2020, so the PS5 menu may have changed since.

findings.label: Where trigger effects and haptics apply
findings.value: 'Haptic feedback and adaptive triggers may require USB connection and are available when supported by game.'; price $74.00, 'Currently Unavailable'
findings.note: Sony's footnote. On PC, adaptive-trigger effects only run in games that support them.

findings.label: Face button type vs G7 Pro / Cyclone 2
findings.value: G7 SE 'Membrane (Quiet/Soft)'; G7 Pro 'Optical Micro Switches'; Cyclone 2 'Mechanical Micro Switches'
findings.source_title: GameSir G7 Pro vs G7 SE vs Gamesir Cyclone 2 (HLPLANET)
findings.note: A cited rival page already states this, so it is not new. It gives no dB figures.
